note_tweet.text:
Who will win personal agents?

🥇 $GOOGL
🥈 $META 
🥉 AI infra supply chain

1) Google will be the biggest winner as all they have to do is flip a switch and use something like "security" or "privacy" as the reason to give their own agents a massive advantage within Gmail and Google Calendar and boom they just won a majority of the market as controlling emails and calendars (and contacts) is the absolute key for every user trying to increase their productivity. These users are very happy to pay and sticky, similar to B2B customers.

2) Because Meta can do the same via WhatsApp they will win on the actual consumer / B2C side. They have the massive distribution, the compute and the perfect application (WhatsApp) to scale consumer use cases. WhatsApp already is like a better version of Google business in many countries. Having your own agent(s) sit in WhatsApp as chats that do things for you like message people, plan things or soon buy things for you, is an easy win for Meta.

3) Then there will probably be a huge and fragmented market across all the companies and use cases where exclusive data exists like finance (you might for example have a dedicated agent for your bank account). Here the main winners will be companies like $NBIS $BE and all the $DRAM stocks that enable the infra of the entire ecosystem.

Another honorable mention in bucket 3) is of course $SPCX with Grok Bot. Great example for this category as even just exclusive data on X is enough to get a significant edge for use cases such as X sentiment tracking, community management, news monitoring, etc.

I'm building what I hope becomes the best daily brief ever.

I run a team of Grok Bots, and each one owns an area: tech and security, social media and news, entertainment and shows, and my inbox and calendar. They watch their area around the clock, spot what matters and act on it. Handing the best of it to my PA bot to pull into my morning brief was the natural next step.

Your What's New bot adds Grok Bot updates too. Thanks for that one!

The brief is smart and personal. The weather shows wind direction and gusts the way I like them. Shows and events suit where my calendar says I'll be. Every news story, film or show with a video has it embedded, ready to watch. It lands as a page in my own app, @artyfaxio, before I wake up.

Every bot learns from my feedback. It feels less like a newsletter and more like a team that knows me.

I've tried building this brief with Claude and Dot too, but Grok Bot is taking it to the next level, and it's been really fun.

note_tweet.text:
这两天随口问了一句大家用 Grok Bot 做什么，没想到收到 180多条回复，挺意外的，也跟大家学到了很多，谢谢大家🙏

我先让 Grok Bot 把所有的评论内容分好类，再从里面挑了 8 个，都是能直接照着试的。

1、每天的 X 运营节奏交给它
早上推选题和值得互动的热帖，晚上给一份当天复盘，周日还可以整理周报和下周计划。比我自己排得还勤快😂
@Cedar3232 

2、开车、午休时用语音聊
上下文一直连着，聊完直接整理成文稿。他在公司做的一次分享，从头到尾都是这样聊出来的。这个我挺想试试。
@conanfighterai

3、一个主 Bot 派活，几个 Bot 分工
按 iPhone 侧键唤起主 Bot，随口说一句行程，它转给助理 Bot，到时间前在微信上提醒。他还专门给孩子配了一个排学习计划的 Bot。
@XIjie5

4、生活里的每件大事，各配一个 Bot
投资、买房、备孕、备考，一件事一个 Bot 盯着，Bot 之间还能互相沟通。看到这条有点感动，是真的在用AI过日子。
@xianyufree

5、给它一个邮箱订 newsletter
资讯都发到这个邮箱，它整理好定时推给你，相当于一个只给自己看的信息流。
@OmegAlphApollo

6、让它帮你打理邮箱
授权后帮你归档邮件、写回复草稿，他说这是最好用的。他还给 Bot 单独开了个邮箱，专门用来注册网站做测试。
@raymondzhang

7、每天盯竞品和用户反馈
做产品营销的朋友，每天让它看竞品动态和用户反馈，整理成日报。
@cherria_okx

8、每天翻一遍评论区，挑出值得回的
评论多了确实翻不过来，这条我太需要了哈哈
@libuyu52413

评论区还有几条上手建议，我觉得很受用：
· 先挑一件每天都在重复的小事交给它 @conanfighterai 

· 先拿能逐项核对的小任务试试它靠不靠谱，比如整理周末活动，让它附上原始链接 @Barry001_

· 发帖、花钱、对外发消息、删东西，这几类事一定要自己把控。他还分享了自己的整套配置，15 条规则、14 个 Bot @zhu1894341

也有朋友提醒，查资料可以，判断别交给它 @Sacmenon。这句我同意，关键的地方我自己把关，剩下的交给它跑。

明天就是1024程序员节了，先提前祝大家节日快乐🎉也想顺便问问大家，你们用AI有没有哪个特别顺手的小技巧？评论区聊聊吧。

虽然现在Grok Bot 真的很好用，大家的评论，每一条我都会看😊

It's twelve AI agents on Grok Bot, each with one job. Vito is my chief of staff. He runs the day and routes work to the others. The rest cover my schedule, household finances, investing, compliance and tax, health, social, and the tools that connect it all.

Tony runs the books for our short-term rental. Bank and card feeds flow into QuickBooks on their own. Every weekday a routine pulls receipts and bills out of the rental's inbox and files them. Tony matches each transaction to its receipt, proposes the category, and checks that QuickBooks ties to the bank. Nothing posts until I approve it. Then he posts it with the receipt attached. He has his own QuickBooks user and never uses my login. A separate compliance agent audits the books every month.

Every agent stays in its lane, only gets the access its job needs, and nothing goes out without my approval.

I CAN’T F*CKING BELIEVE IT, BUT ELON MUSK REPOSTED BOTH OF MY GROK BOT SETUPS.

IF ELON APPROVED THEM, THEY’RE WORTH TRYING FOR EVERYONE.

Here are the two setups.

→ CONTENT GROK BOT SETUP: I use it every day in my work.

A Chief of Staff routes every task to six agents. One researches what’s moving, one writes, one creates visuals in my style, one checks the numbers, one schedules and one publishes. They share memory, so the research is already inside the draft before the draft starts.

The result: I post consistently without spending my day switching between six different jobs.

→ TRAVEL GROK BOT SETUP: I use it to plan and book my trips.

I asked it to plan, research and book my trip to Lisbon. The agents searched for flights and stays, compared prices and total costs, then completed the bookings with my card and turned everything into one itinerary.

I only had to ask, and my trip was booked.

Grok Bot has become my main tool every single day, for work and for everything else. Content, research, travel, shopping, life admin: I hand it the task and it gets done. The range of what it can do is huge.

Every agent gets its own computer, browser and memory, it keeps working while I’m offline, and it can even learn a task by watching me do it once. It’s the first tool that actually gives me time back instead of adding more work.

That’s why I think everyone should try bringing it into their daily life. Start with my ready-made setups, or build your own around the way you live and work.
